paper.title_en: Regular Reissner--Nordström--de Sitter Black Holes: Thin-Shell Matching and Modified Density Profiles
paper.abstract_en: We investigate two distinct approaches to regularizing the central singularity of the Reissner--Nordström--de Sitter geometry. In the first approach, a de Sitter interior is matched to an exact Reissner--Nordström--de Sitter exterior across a timelike dust shell. Using the Israel junction conditions, we derive the effective potential governing the shell dynamics and analyze its static equilibrium and radial stability. We show that radial stability requires $Λ_->Λ_+$, while the additional requirement of three distinct exterior horizons, with the shell located inside the inner horizon, leads to the stronger analytical result that such stable black-hole configurations exist if and only if $Λ_->3Λ_+$. We also derive an upper bound on the exterior mass parameter and recover the Reissner--Nordström limit as $Λ_+\to0$. Although the singular center is replaced by a regular core, the stationary exterior geometry remains unchanged, demonstrating that exterior geometric observations alone cannot determine whether the black-hole interior is singular or regular. In the second approach, we modify the divergent energy-density profile and reconstruct a smooth geometry with a de Sitter core while preserving the Reissner--Nordström--de Sitter asymptotics. Regularity fixes the smoothing scale to $β=Q^2/(2m)$, leaving no independent regularization parameter. The two constructions thus provide distinct regularization mechanisms, rather than equivalent descriptions of the same spacetime.
